title: How Forward Deployed Engineering is done at Decagon — Sunny Rekhi

primary.label: Agent Architecture & Harnesses
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 51%).

domains.label: Customer Support
domains.rationale: Decagon's product is explicitly an AI customer support agent replacing IVR phone trees and slow email responses. The entire talk is about deploying, configuring, and scaling this customer support agent for enterprise brands.

domains.label: Enterprise Operations
domains.rationale: The talk covers enterprise deployment practices, forward deployed engineering processes, scaling engineering teams from 50 to 500, and operational practices like knowledge sharing across deployments and agent compounding.

summary: Sunny Rekhi, CTO of Forward Deployed Engineering at Decagon, presents how Decagon builds and deploys 24/7 multilingual, omni-channel AI customer service agents for enterprise brands. The talk covers the two forms of forward deployed work: configuring the agent brain (instructions, brand tonality, action mappings, human handoff rules) and front-line product engineering that anticipates recurring customer needs across enterprises. Rekhi argues that forward deployed engineering and product engineering have become indistinguishable at Decagon, sharing the same bar, reporting structure, and often the same team—because a Fortune 20 pain point is typically a product feature waiting to be built. He describes how scaling from 50 to 500 people in one year split the generalist agent software engineer role into agent builders (UI-driven configuration, model intuition) and agent software engineers (product feature incorporation). A central theme is that with AI coding tools now strong, the scarce skill is restraint—resisting one-off patches in favor of solutions architected to scale to future customers. The guiding ethos 'custom becomes self-serve' is illustrated by Decagon building approximately 25 custom CRM integrations before productizing them into a self-serve system, so work that once required an engineer is now done by customers or the agent building team. Rekhi emphasizes defining success metrics in writing during the earliest deal conversations, proving value fast in multi-year partnerships where trust is won in the first weeks, and acting as both executor and advisor—using cross-customer pattern knowledge to recommend highest-ROI automations, even when they differ from what the customer initially requested. The Hertz case study shows the land-and-expand model: starting with inbound support deflection, then expanding to proactive lease-renewal outreach using existing backend integrations. At 500-person scale, rigorous knowledge sharing ensures the agent compounds: improvements made for one customer benefit all future customers.
whyItMatters: The software engineering and AI concepts in this talk form a tightly coupled narrative about how to build and scale an AI agent company. The AI concepts—agent brain configuration, AI customer service agents, agent compounding, and AI coding tools—define what is being built and the technical substrate. The software engineering concepts—forward deployed engineering, productization, role specialization, restraint, success metrics, proving value fast, knowledge compounding, and the advisor role—define how that building is organized, scaled, and sustained. The critical insight is that these two domains are inseparable at Decagon: forward deployed engineering IS product engineering because the act of configuring an AI agent for one enterprise customer reveals product features needed by all future customers. The 'custom becomes self-serve' ethos is the bridge: it starts as an AI agent configuration task (agent brain configuration) performed by a forward deployed engineer, and through restraint and productization, becomes a platform feature that non-engineers can use. AI coding tools accelerate this loop by making code production fast, but restraint ensures the output scales. Agent compounding is the payoff: each deployment's learnings, upstreamed through productization and shared through knowledge compounding, make every future deployment faster and the AI agent smarter. Without the engineering practices (metrics upfront, proving value fast, advisor role), the AI concepts would remain one-off deployments; without the AI concepts, the engineering practices would lack a compounding substrate to apply them to.
temporalContext: The video was published on July 28, 2026, capturing a talk delivered at the AI Engineer World's Fair 2026. Research was conducted as of August 22, 2026. At the time of the talk, Decagon had recently crossed $100M+ ARR (confirmed by Newcomer in August 2026) and was valued at $4.5B following a $250M Series D in January 2026 (Bloomberg). Sunny Rekhi had been in his CTO of FDE role since May 2026, approximately two months before the talk. The scaling narrative—from 50 to 500 people in one year—reflects Decagon's hyper-growth period during 2025-2026, roughly two and a half years after the company's founding in August 2023. The talk reflects the state of AI agent deployment practices at a moment when AI coding tools (Codex, Claude Code) had become strong enough to change engineering workflows, and when the FDE role was being widely adopted across the AI industry.
takeaways: Forward deployed engineering and product engineering are treated as identical at Decagon—same bar, same reporting, same team—because a customer pain point is usually a product feature waiting to be built.
The forward deployed role has two halves: configuring the agent brain and acting as front-line product engineering that anticipates recurring customer asks.
Scaling from 50 to 500 people split the generalist agent software engineer into agent builders (UI-driven configuration) and agent software engineers (product feature incorporation).
With AI coding tools now strong, the scarce skill is restraint—resisting one-off patches in favor of solutions architected to scale to future customers.
'Custom becomes self-serve' is the guiding ethos: after building 25 custom integrations, Decagon productized them so future customers inherit capabilities for free.
Forward deployed engineers must be advisors, not just executors—using cross-customer pattern knowledge to recommend highest-ROI automations, even when they differ from the customer's initial request.
Proving value fast is critical: relationships are multi-year but trust is won in the first weeks, so the motion must demonstrate value ASAP rather than over months.
Success metrics should be defined and put in writing during the earliest deal conversations to keep both parties aligned.
At 500-person scale, knowledge sharing across deployments is rigorous, ensuring the agent compounds—improvements for one customer benefit all future customers.

concepts.name: Agent brain configuration
concepts.explanation: Configuring LLM-based AI agents through natural-language instructions, brand tonality settings, action mappings (tool use), and human handoff rules. This is one of the two primary forms of forward deployed work at Decagon, performed by agent builders using UI-driven tools.
concepts.importance: This is the core technical activity that makes Decagon's AI agents operational for specific enterprise customers. It represents the configuration layer that sits between the base LLM and the customer-facing agent behavior.

concepts.name: AI customer service agents
concepts.explanation: 24/7 multilingual, omni-channel AI agents that replace IVR phone trees and slow email responses with human-like replies. They unify chat, voice, email, and SMS support for enterprise customers, handling complex inbound support workflows and expanding into proactive revenue-generating use cases.
concepts.importance: This is Decagon's core product and the deployment context for all the engineering practices discussed. The Hertz case study demonstrates how an AI support agent can expand from reactive deflection to proactive outreach.

concepts.name: Agent compounding
concepts.explanation: The principle that improvements made to the AI agent for one customer's deployment benefit all future customers. At 500-person scale, Decagon ensures the agent compounds every time it interfaces with a customer, through rigorous knowledge sharing and upstreaming of field insights into the platform.
concepts.importance: This is the scaling flywheel for AI agent products: each deployment makes the platform better for the next, creating a moat that compounds over time and justifies the upfront investment in productization.

concepts.name: AI coding tools changing engineering skill requirements
concepts.explanation: With AI coding tools like Codex and Claude Code now strong enough to one-off fix things quickly, the scarce engineering skill has shifted from writing code to exercising judgment about what to build and how it scales. This changes the bar for forward deployed engineers.
concepts.importance: This concept explains why restraint became the defining skill: AI tools have commoditized the ability to produce code quickly, making architectural thinking and product judgment the differentiators.

concepts.name: Forward Deployed Engineering
concepts.explanation: A software engineering practice where engineers are embedded directly with enterprise customers to deploy, configure, and build custom solutions on-site. At Decagon, the FDE role encompasses two functions: configuring the agent brain and acting as front-line product engineering that anticipates recurring customer asks.
concepts.importance: This is the central organizing concept of the talk. Rekhi describes how FDE at Decagon has converged with product engineering, dissolving the traditional boundary between customer-facing deployment work and platform development.

concepts.name: Productization of custom work (custom becomes self-serve)
concepts.explanation: The practice of identifying recurring custom engineering patterns and transforming them into reusable, configurable platform features. After building ~25 custom CRM integrations, Decagon productized them into a self-serve system so customers or agent builders can configure integrations without engineering involvement.
concepts.importance: This is Decagon's guiding ethos and the mechanism by which FDE work scales. Every manual step gets upstreamed into the product so future customers inherit capabilities for free, reducing the need for manual intervention over time.

concepts.name: Role specialization during organizational scaling
concepts.explanation: As a company scales, generalist engineering roles split into specialized sub-roles. At Decagon, the generalist agent software engineer split into agent builders (UI-driven configuration, model intuition) and agent software engineers (product feature incorporation) when the company grew from 50 to 500 people.
concepts.importance: This illustrates how engineering org structures must evolve with scale, and how the introduction of AI tools and self-serve systems creates new specialized roles while reducing the need for others.

concepts.name: Restraint as an engineering discipline
concepts.explanation: With AI coding tools (Codex, Claude Code) now strong, the temptation is to one-off fix things quickly. The scarce skill is exercising restraint—thinking about how a solution scales to future customers and avoiding brittle black-box prompts and patches.
concepts.importance: Rekhi positions restraint as the defining engineering skill in the age of AI-assisted coding. It directly ties to the productization ethos: without restraint, engineers accumulate technical debt through one-off solutions that never become platform features.

concepts.name: Success metrics definition upfront
concepts.explanation: Defining what success looks like for the customer—metrics, channels, pain points, ideal outcomes—and ideally getting it in writing during the earliest deal conversations, before any building begins.
concepts.importance: This is a requirements engineering practice that ensures alignment between the FDE team and the customer, preventing scope drift and misaligned expectations in multi-year partnerships.

concepts.name: Proving value fast in enterprise deployments
concepts.explanation: In enterprise deals, forward deployed engineers must demonstrate value as fast as possible rather than over months. Trust is won in the first weeks of a multi-year relationship, so the deployment motion must show ROI quickly before expanding scope.
concepts.importance: This shapes the entire deployment strategy: start with a focused, high-impact use case, prove value, then expand into broader support and revenue-generating workflows.

concepts.name: Knowledge compounding across deployments
concepts.explanation: Staffing the same core group of industry experts across similar vertical deals compounds knowledge, credibility, and ramp-up speed. At 500-person scale, Decagon rigorously shares knowledge across deployments so improvements for one customer benefit all future customers.
concepts.importance: This is the scaling mechanism that makes the productization ethos sustainable. Without systematic knowledge sharing, each deployment would start from scratch and custom work would never get upstreamed.

concepts.name: Advisor vs executor role for engineers
concepts.explanation: Forward deployed engineers should treat themselves as advisors as well as executors. Decagon ingests customers' historical support data and recommends where the highest-ROI automation lies, which sometimes differs from what the customer initially requested. Cross-customer pattern knowledge is a valuable asset.
concepts.importance: This redefines the FDE role from a pure implementation function to a strategic advisory one, where the engineer's cross-customer perspective becomes a competitive advantage.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.summary: Sunny Rekhi introduces himself as CTO of Forward Deployed Engineering at Decagon and outlines the talk: what forward deployed work is, why Decagon has it, how it changed scaling from 50 to 500 people, and differences between Fortune 20 and mid-market brands.

sections.title: What Decagon's support agent does
sections.summary: Decagon is a 24/7 multilingual, omni-channel AI customer service agent that replaces phone trees and slow email responses with human-like replies. It lands to help with complex support workflows and expands into proactive revenue-generating use cases.

sections.title: Hertz: offloading support to proactive outreach
sections.summary: Hertz came for inbound support deflection. Once Decagon had backend integrations, it expanded to proactively reaching out to customers for lease renewals and extensions, turning a support tool into a revenue driver.

sections.title: Two kinds of forward deployed work
sections.summary: First kind: configuring the agent brain—instructions, tonality, actions, and human handoff rules. Second kind: front-line product engineering, anticipating that enterprise A's ask will recur at enterprises B through E and solving it for all of them proactively.

sections.title: Forward deployed engineering equals product engineering
sections.summary: At Decagon the line between forward deployed and product engineering is gone—same bar, same reporting, often same team. A Fortune 20 pain point expressed to a forward deployed engineer is usually a product feature that needs prioritization.

sections.title: Scaling from 50 to 500 people
sections.summary: At 50 people, generalist agent software engineers did everything—agent configuration, backend integration, and platform work. At 500, the role split into agent builders (UI-driven configuration, model intuition) and agent software engineers (front-line product request incorporation).

sections.title: Restraint as the scarce skill
sections.summary: With AI coding tools now strong, the temptation is to one-off fix things with Codex or Claude Code. The scarce skill is exercising restraint—thinking about how a solution scales to future customers and avoiding brittle black-box prompts and patches.

sections.title: Ramping a new enterprise deal
sections.summary: Success must be defined early—metrics, channels, pain points, ideal outcomes—and ideally put in writing. There is now significant upfront effort in requirements gathering before building, which is a shift driven by AI coding changing engineering generally.

sections.title: Industry experts and compounding knowledge
sections.summary: Staffing the same core group of industry experts across similar vertical deals compounds knowledge, credibility, and ramp-up speed, making each deployment faster than the last.

sections.title: Solving a problem so it scales
sections.summary: Forward deployed engineers should always think about how to solve a customer problem in a way that extends to other customers and empowers the rest of the business. Decagon's ethos is that agents should be configurable via natural language, so engineering work gets upstreamed into the product.

sections.title: Custom integrations become self-serve
sections.summary: Rekhi describes how Decagon repeatedly built custom CRM integrations—after roughly 25 of them, the team decided to build a self-serve system. Work that once required an engineer writing custom code can now be done by customers or the agent building team.

sections.title: Proving value fast
sections.summary: In enterprise deals, forward deployed engineers must prove value as fast as possible. Decagon could become arbitrarily complex, but the goal is to demonstrate value ASAP rather than over months. Once value is proven, the relationship expands into broader support and revenue-generating workflows across a multi-year partnership.

sections.title: Advisor, not just executor
sections.summary: Forward deployed engineers should treat themselves as advisors as well as executors. Decagon ingests customers' historical support data and recommends where the highest ROI automation lies, which sometimes differs from what the customer initially requested. The cross-customer pattern knowledge is a valuable asset.

sections.title: Custom becomes self-serve as guiding ethos
sections.summary: Every time something is done manually, Decagon tries to upstream it into the product. 'Custom becomes self-serve' has become a guiding ethos for the forward deployed team, and Rekhi encourages everyone on the front lines to keep this top of mind.

sections.title: What Decagon did right and designing the system at scale
sections.summary: Decagon earned its position by moving fast on customer asks, building trust as advisors not just executors, and productizing custom work. At 500 people, the focus shifted to designing the system: rigorously sharing knowledge across deployments, feeding field insights back to the platform, and ensuring the agent compounds—improvements for one customer benefit all future customers.

organization.name: Decagon
organization.summary: Decagon is a San Francisco-based conversational AI company founded in August 2023 by Jesse Zhang and Ashwin Sreenivas. The company builds AI customer service agents that provide 24/7 support across voice, chat, email, and SMS channels. Decagon's platform includes Agent Operating Procedures (AOPs) for defining agent workflows in natural language, testing and QA tools, experimentation capabilities, and analytics. The company serves enterprise customers across multiple industries including retail, travel, technology, financial services, health and wellness, media, and telecommunications. Notable customers include Avis Budget Group, Chime, Oura Health, 1-800-FLOWERS.COM, Hunter Douglas, Notion, Eventbrite, Duolingo, and others. As of August 2026, Decagon has approximately 390 employees, has raised $481M in total funding at a $4.5B valuation, and has crossed $100M in annualized revenue. The company is backed by investors including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures.
organization.status: Active and rapidly growing. As of August 2026, Decagon has approximately 390 employees (up from approximately 50 a year prior), has raised $481M in total funding at a $4.5 billion valuation, and has crossed $100 million in annualized revenue.

technologies.label: Decagon AI Agent Platform
technologies.primary: Decagon AI customer service agent platform
technologies.summary: Decagon's AI customer service agent platform is a 24/7 multilingual, omni-channel AI system that replaces IVR phone trees and slow email responses with human-like replies. It unifies chat, voice, email, and SMS support for enterprise customers, handling complex inbound support workflows and expanding into proactive revenue-generating use cases such as Hertz lease renewal outreach. The platform is designed so that improvements for one customer compound across all future deployments through rigorous knowledge sharing and upstreaming of field insights.
technologies.role: This is the core product being deployed, configured, and scaled throughout the talk. All forward deployed engineering practices discussed (agent brain configuration, productization, restraint, advisor role) are in service of building and deploying this platform for enterprise customers.

technologies.label: Agent Brain Configuration Architecture
technologies.summary: Agent brain configuration is the architecture for customizing LLM-based AI agents through natural-language instructions, brand tonality settings, action mappings (tool use), and human handoff rules. At Decagon, this is one of two primary forms of forward deployed work, performed by agent builders using UI-driven tools after the role split from generalist agent software engineers during scaling. The configuration layer sits between the base LLM and the customer-facing agent behavior, enabling non-engineers to customize agent behavior for specific enterprise customers without writing code.
technologies.role: Described as one of two primary forms of forward deployed engineering work at Decagon, central to how agents are customized for enterprise customers without requiring software engineering for each deployment.

technologies.label: Self-serve Integration Platform
technologies.summary: After building approximately 25 custom CRM integrations as one-off engineering work, Decagon productized them into a self-serve integration platform. This system allows customers or agent builders to configure integrations without engineering involvement, embodying the 'custom becomes self-serve' ethos. The self-serve system reduces the need for forward deployed engineers on routine integration work and ensures future customers inherit capabilities for free. Decagon's own engineering blog reports that restructuring forward deployment into Agent Development cut custom engineering work per agent by 80%.
technologies.role: Serves as the primary case study for Decagon's 'custom becomes self-serve' productization ethos, illustrating how custom engineering work gets upstreamed into platform features that non-engineers can use.

technologies.label: AI Coding Tools
technologies.summary: AI-assisted coding tools like OpenAI Codex and Anthropic's Claude Code have become strong enough to produce code quickly, changing the engineering skill landscape. In the video, Rekhi notes that with these tools, the scarce skill is no longer writing code fast but exercising restraint—resisting one-off patches and brittle black-box prompts in favor of solutions architected to scale to future customers. These tools are mentioned as contextual technology that explains why the engineering discipline of restraint has become critical for forward deployed engineers.
technologies.role: Mentioned as contextual technology that explains why restraint became the defining scarce skill for forward deployed engineers at Decagon and across the AI industry.
